study.question: Does centered real-label auxiliary supervision help history learning after separating operation-order and precision effects from its expected-permutation regularization control? Observed starting point: baseline-static/pooled/din AUCs are 0.60500361/0.61022611/0.61336199. The incumbent g3-r0001-expected_permuted reaches 0.61363367, a preliminary single-seed gain of 0.00027168. However, g3-r0004-aligned_learned is 0.61313311 versus 0.61346391 for g3-r0004-expected_control; the blocked arm exactly returns baseline-din. The expected control records train_centered_gap_mean=-0.0021439326 despite the mathematical Jensen nonnegativity constraint, raw validation logit mean=-132.00945 and head shape drift=18.15277. This is an unresolved objective-integrity limitation, not established evidence that the real-label mechanism fails. Parent sources and baseline hashes were verified; raw data and host trainer are not exported, and no local baseline execution is authorized.
study.hypothesis: Left-associative float32 c+z-mean(z) can violate common-shift invariance as the learned head drifts, potentially contaminating the null trajectory and its contrast with label alignment. Computing u=z-mean(z) before c+u, with float64 promotion before every scalar mean/offset/loss operation, should restore the declared objective within tolerance. Conditional scientific hypothesis: aligned supervision C-A can then improve primary validation AUC over the equally implemented null C by at least 0.0001 without changing inference computation. The arithmetic repair is an implementation correction to existing objectives, not a claimed new mathematical training signal. The real-label versus permutation-expectation contrast is the mechanism distinction; this is a discriminating continuation of an unsuccessful implementation. Synthetic stdlib float32-rounding checks established susceptibility only: q=.052, z=-100000+[-.0625,0,.0625] yields legacy gap -9.89747e-5 versus center-first fp64 gap +6.42022e-5 when softplus/reduction are computed in real-valued Python arithmetic. Those values do not recreate GPU kernels, actual training batches or gradients. A saved validation mean of -132 alone does not explain a training average gap of -0.00214.

nearest_work.difference: Inherit the real-label centered C-A objective, learned head, mask and frozen prediction graph from source sha256 7fd55901e402fdfb95a8ae2d4cbf7fbb93f9a565dfa2e9bb2226d99e32c56ed7. Change scalar arithmetic to center first in fp64 and add training-only invariant telemetry. This is no new objective or architectural novelty claim.

Source sha256 1f4d280fe5ae10ff58572fd526476e173349dd2dff8cb4aaad3ae68ba39c7d73 confirms c+z-m in fp32 and reports a negative training gap. Introduce a center-first fp32 replacement plus a center-first fp64 replacement; source replays diagnose arithmetic on the same training logits without claiming a trained-model counterfactual.

This study changes training-only pooled-history auxiliary arithmetic, not DIN activation, normalization or its regularizer.

study.proposed_difference: Register four standalone modules: stable_aligned (candidate.py, C-A in center-first fp64), stable_expected (C in center-first fp64), reordered_expected (C in center-first fp32), stable_blocked (C-A in center-first fp64, detach pooled only on the auxiliary path). The first pair isolates observed-label alignment versus its exact expected-label null. The next pair isolates scalar precision after parenthesization is fixed. Existing g3-r0004-expected_control supplies the legacy-operation control with the same backbone/seed/head; summaries change but do not enter gradients. The blocked arm checks the primary trajectory and auxiliary gradient dependence. Full fp64 is limited to B-sized auxiliary scalars; backbone and head parameters remain fp32. All arms record example-weighted chosen/legacy/reordered gaps, same-logit legacy-versus-fp64 discrepancies, negative-gap minima/fraction, centering errors and raw-mean maxima from TRAINING only. No gap clamp or penalty is added. Diagnostics have 46 named scalars under the host limit of 64. The archived negative receipt remains intact; this proposal appends a hypothesis and revision rather than overwriting it. Broad novelty remains unverified; registry searches for regularization/floating-point found no additional nearest papers.
predictions: Integrity prediction: center-first fp64 chosen training gap never falls below -1e-8 on nonempty batches, and train_center_error_abs_max is below 1e-8. These are numerical tolerances, not performance thresholds. No clipping is used to manufacture this property.

Attribution prediction: on trajectories with large common-shift logits, legacy_center_error and legacy_vs_fp64_gap discrepancies increase; center-first fp32 reduces the operation-order error. If actual trajectories never enter that regime, rounding is not supported as a consequential explanation of the archived result.

Performance prediction, preliminary seed 42: stable_aligned AUC exceeds stable_expected by >=0.0001. Compare unweighted Logloss too, and require no >0.0001 deterioration in Logloss for practical preference. AUC alone cannot establish a representation mechanism.

Routing prediction: stable_blocked reproduces baseline-din AUC 0.6133619861190683 and Logloss 0.19679464647483236 within 1e-7. Exact equality is expected under the host deterministic recipe; a mismatch triggers a source/RNG/optimizer audit before attribution.

Efficiency prediction: inference graph and parameter allocation match the parent (17,130,852 total parameters including the unused 577-parameter training head), but wall time and GPU seconds must be measured. Aim for <=25% wall overhead relative to ~611 s recent trials; exceeding that makes efficiency unsupported even if integrity improves. Training diagnostic buffers add 112 bytes relative to the five-double parent summary, and contribute no learned capacity.

All host slices are exploratory unless separately predeclared, with their sample/positive/negative counts retained. One seed and first-512-input candidate diagnostics cannot justify significance, broad mechanism support or transfer.
falsifiers: A fp64 chosen gap below -1e-8, large center error, nonfinite logits/loss/diagnostics, or blocked-control primary mismatch falsifies the proposed integrity restoration; retain the failed receipt and do not claim a mechanism result.

Stable aligned-minus-null AUC <=0 fails the directional performance hypothesis; an improvement below 0.0001 fails the predeclared practical threshold. If the null matches or beats the aligned candidate, prefer the simpler supported interpretation of regularization over task-aligned representation learning.

If training same-logit legacy-versus-fp64 errors are negligible and arithmetic interventions do not change relevant outcomes, the numerical explanation is unsupported. Do not retroactively attribute the earlier negative diagnostic to rounding without evidence.
If only raw logits or head norms change, but full-population AUC/Logloss and useful slices do not improve, a geometry change alone does not establish better history utility.

If seed-43/44 paired repeats reverse the improvement or intervals remain compatible with no useful effect, retain a preliminary or null conclusion. Costs/throughput cannot be inferred from identical inference source alone.
alternative_explanations: The negative archived training gap could arise from a diagnostic/accumulation error, unexpected precision or another unavailable host behavior. No saved training batches are exposed, so the cause is presently unresolved.

The saved validation raw mean=-132 is not the maximum common shift over training. The synthetic audit only demonstrates mathematical susceptibility of one operation order and does not reproduce the archived scalar.

Auxiliary learning may mostly regularize shared category/brand embeddings rather than encode useful history-specific information; unchanged inference and a blocked-gradient control identify gradient influence but not its representation location.

Real click labels are sparse/noisy, static features may already explain their predictable component, and forcing a history-only pooled head to predict clicks may remain harmful even with correct arithmetic.

Changing scalar precision changes q/c rounding, loss reduction, the gradient projection and optimizer trajectories together. The fp32 reorder control isolates order on the null; this four-arm suite does not fully factorialize precision x alignment. If this interaction matters, add a center-first fp32 aligned arm prospectively with reserved resources.

The learned head can collapse its sensitivity or drift even with mathematically shift-invariant losses. Numeric validity is necessary for this interpretation, not sufficient for history representation quality.

Single-seed validation adaptivity, checkpoint selection, stochastic seed variation and ordinary regularization can explain small AUC differences. Paired repeated seeds and user-cluster uncertainty are required when available.

Publisher static attributes have undocumented as-of dates; the frozen benchmark assumption remains unverified for production causality. Coarse category/brand histories cannot stand in for unavailable item histories or conversion-delay supervision.
